fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the CoCrFeNi matrix with an equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy and does not investigate Mo variation or the Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
It does not address coefficient of friction or wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed intervention, processing window, and phase constitution are unrelated to the target intervention and SPS conditions.
The mechanism concerns bulk strengthening rather than low-temperature solid-lubricant films and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate tribofilms.
No relevant sliding load, counterface, speed, distance, atmosphere, or temperature-dependent wear boundaries are specified.
The falsification experiment measures only hardness and phase fractions, so it cannot test the claimed solution to the wide-temperature tribology problem.
explanation: The response is essentially a hypothesis for strengthening a mechanically alloyed CoCrFeNiTi bulk alloy, not for achieving wide-temperature self-lubrication in CoCrFeNi. It omits the relevant Mo-containing Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite, the RT–800 °C sliding tests, and the transition from MoS2/Ag lubrication to oxide and silver-molybdate glaze formation. Its hardness/XRD experiment has limited ability to test its own structural claims but cannot discriminate tribological performance against the starting material. The approach is conventional and unsupported by citations.
